ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure shows a transition-state structure, containing an upper O-H substituent, a carbonyl fragment on the right and a terminal methyl group, and below there is also an oxygen-containing carbon chain/cyclic fragment; there are also multiple curved arrows in the figure, but the problem requires ignoring the arrows. Then reason: Count only connections between non-hydrogen atoms; the O-H bond is not counted. Enumerating one by one according to the structure in the figure: the O-C bond between the upper O and the central C is 1; the C=C in the central carbon skeleton is 1; the single bond from that alkene carbon to the carbonyl carbon is 1; the carbonyl C=O is 1; the C-C bond from the carbonyl carbon to the terminal methyl carbon on the right is 1. Continue counting the lower fragment: the left O-C bond is 1; the adjacent C-C bond is 1; the lower C=C bond is 1; and the C-C bond back to the central carbon is 1. The total is 1+1+1+1+1+1+1+1+1=9.

raw_record.question_text: In the transition-state structure shown in the image, calculate the total number of bonds in the structure, including single, double, and triple bonds but excluding those involving hydrogen. Note: Disregard arrows. Consider all components present in the transition-state structure shown in the image.

method.method_draft: Directly enumerate every non-hydrogen bond visible in the transition-state structure. Ignore the curved arrows. Starting from the top O-H substituent, count the O-C bond but not the O-H bond. Continue through the carbon skeleton to count the alkene C=C connection, the single bond to the carbonyl carbon, the carbonyl C=O connection, and the bond to the terminal methyl carbon. Then count the lower fragment connections: left O-C, C-C, C=C, and C-C back to the central carbon. Total these distinct non-H interatomic connections to obtain 9.

method.method_draft: Model the drawing as a graph whose nodes are all non-hydrogen atoms. Assign non-H degrees from the visible skeleton: top O has degree 1; upper carbon degree 2; central carbon degree 3; carbonyl carbon degree 3; carbonyl O degree 1; terminal carbon degree 1; left O degree 1; lower-left carbon degree 2; lower-middle carbon degree 2; lower-right carbon degree 2. The degree sum is 18, and dividing by 2 gives 9 total non-H bonds.
